newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Durban Deep slides after revision of ratios.
newsitem.headline: Durban Deep slides after revision of ratios.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Durban Roodepooort Deep Ltd tumbled on Wednesday after Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd revised ratios for the proposed West Rand merger of its three gold mines.
The mines are Buffelsfontein Gold Mining Co Ltd, Blyvooruitzicht Gold Mining Co Ltd and Durban Deep. Dealers said the prices were coming into line with the new ratios.
"Durban Deep is down on the recalculation of the ratios. The prices are coming into line with the new ratios," a dealer said.
Durban Deep dropped 24.24 percent, or 3.20 rand, to 10 rand in a volume of just under a million rand's worth.

Randgold said on Tuesday Buffels shareholders will now be entitled to 110 Durban Deep ordinary shares per 100 shares held and Blyvoor shareholders to 25 per 100. The original ratios were 77 per 100 in the case of Buffels and 20 in the case of Blyvoor.
The terms for the Blyvoor options remain unchanged at 20 new Durban Deep options per 100.
Blyvoor shares also lost 25 cents to 250 cents, Buffels shares cut 50 cents to 960 cents and Randgold shares were down 70 cents to 15.80 rand.
Randgold announced earlier this month that it planned to revise the merger ratios.
Chairman Roger Kebble said the decision to revise the ratios had been driven by the downturn in the gold price, which earlier this month hit a 12-year low.
He added that the current depressed state of the market made the case for a merger more compelling than ever.
